best_for: Music collectors with folders of badly tagged MP3 and FLAC files who want them named, tagged and given cover art in one pass.

points.title: It listens to the file
points.text: AcoustID fingerprints identify a track by its audio, so even files with no tags at all can be matched against the MusicBrainz database.

points.title: Tags, renames and sorts
points.text: Picard writes tags, fetches cover art, and can rename and move files into a folder layout you define with its own scripting language. It handles MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A, WMA, WAV and more.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Picard is GPL-2.0-or-later and costs nothing. CD lookups are built in.

points.title: Version 3 breaks old plugins
points.text: Picard 3 has a new plugin system with trust levels, and plugins written for 2.x do not work until someone ports them. If you rely on a niche plugin, check it before upgrading or stay on a 2.x build.

points.title: Mac needs macOS 13
points.text: The Mac builds come in separate Intel and Apple Silicon DMGs, both for macOS 13 or later. The Windows installer installs machine-wide on Windows 10 or 11, x64 only.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 24 versions, which makes going back to Picard 2.x easy there. macOS and Linux list only the current release. The Flathub build, published under the MetaBrainz Foundation name, is not marked verified by Flathub.
